meta.title: Wham - your Mac stays awake, lid closed
meta.description: Close the lid. Your Mac stays awake. A one-click menu bar switch that keeps your Mac awake, for real, even with the lid shut. Free and open source.
meta.keywords: Mac, macOS, keep awake, lid closed, clamshell, menu bar, pmset, caffeinate, Amphetamine alternative

hero.title: Close the lid.
hero.lead: A one-click menu bar switch that keeps your Mac awake, for real, even with the lid shut.
hero.note: Free. macOS 11 or later. Apple silicon and Intel.
hero.stage: A MacBook closes its lid while a long job keeps running: coding agents like Claude Code, a film export, a download, a render, a backup. The lid opens on the finished job.

try.title: One switch in your menu bar.
try.lead: That is the whole app. A sun when your Mac stays awake, a moon when it can sleep, a little chime either way. Go on, click it.

demo.switch: Keep this Mac awake, even with the lid closed
demo.caption: Sound on: that is the real chime, an 8-bit arpeggio played by your browser.

uses.title: Made for long jobs.
uses.lead: Start it, close the lid, walk away. Anything that takes longer than you want to sit and watch keeps going until it is done.

agents.title: AI coding agents
agents.text: Hand Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Grok a long task, close the lid and go. They keep working until it is done.

jobs.title: Exports and renders
jobs.text: Final Cut, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve or Blender, all the way to the last frame.

jobs.title: Downloads and backups
jobs.text: A big model, a fresh Xcode, Time Machine or Backblaze. Close the lid at 3%, open it at 100%.

jobs.title: Remote access
jobs.text: Screen Sharing, SSH, AirPlay to the speakers, the dev server you open on your phone: your Mac still answers.

jobs.title: A home server, 24/7
jobs.text: An old Mac on a shelf, lid shut, up day and night: Plex, Home Assistant or Homebridge, reachable from anywhere.

how.title: Three steps. The third one is the point.

steps.title: Download and open Wham
steps.text: Drag it to Applications and open it. It lives in your menu bar, next to the clock.

steps.title: Click the switch
steps.text: The sun comes out and the chime plays. The very first time, macOS asks for your password, once.

steps.title: Close the lid
steps.text: Your Mac keeps going. Claude Code finishes its task, the export reaches the last frame, the download hits 100%.

how.note: Most keep-awake apps only ask macOS to stay up, which it ignores once the lid closes, so Wham turns sleep off itself and back on when you are done.

tiny.title: You will forget it is running.
tiny.lead: Wham does one thing: every two seconds, it reads one kernel flag. While on, it also listens for the battery, the heat and the lid, which macOS announces. The rest of the time it does nothing at all, and CI holds it to a budget.

stats.text: The whole app, on disk. The download is 2.7 MB.
Of one CPU core, idle: a hundredth of a second of work every 30 seconds.
Dependencies. No analytics, no trackers, no background daemon.

tiny.scale: For scale: KeepingYouAwake takes 7.6 MB on disk, and Amphetamine is a 6.7 MB download before its helper apps. Measured on a MacBook Air, macOS 26.6; the details are in <doc>docs/compatibility.md</doc>.

compare.title: Most keep-awake apps stop at the lid.
compare.lead: Keeping a Mac awake with the lid open is easy. Shut it, and macOS ignores the polite way to ask. Here is how the well-known apps handle a closed lid, on battery, with no screen plugged in.

wham.text: Turns off the kernel's sleep flag, the one switch macOS honors with the lid shut, and back on when you are done: for as long as you say, never down to a flat battery, never past critically hot. Download, drag, click. macOS 11 or later, Intel too, signed and notarized.
wham.meta: 1.4 MB on disk · Free, open source

amphetamine.text: Sandboxed by the App Store. For a closed lid it offers Amphetamine Enhancer, a separate app from outside the store, and on Apple silicon laptops Power Protect, another separate download.

caffeine.text: Holds a power assertion: the polite request to stay up that macOS drops the moment the lid closes.

keepingyouawake.text: A friendly switch for caffeinate. In its own words, it “will only prevent sleep on desktop Macs and portable Macs with an open lid.”
keepingyouawake.meta: 7.6 MB on disk · Free, open source

caffeinate.text: Built into macOS, with the same power assertions. Even its strongest flag, -s, is “valid only when system is running on AC power.”

compare.lungo: On their own, App Store apps cannot, and the honest ones say so: Lungo “will not prevent your computer from sleeping if you close the lid. This is a Mac App Store limitation.”

items.a: No. Download Wham, open it, and everything happens in the menu bar: one click to keep your Mac awake, one click to let it sleep. The commands at the bottom of this page are only there for people who like typing them.

Yes. Turning sleep off takes an administrator: the first time you click, macOS asks for your password once, so Wham can flip the sleep setting without asking again. That is the only thing it is allowed to do. The app is signed by its developer and notarized by Apple, and every line of it is on <github>GitHub</github>.

items.q: Can I turn it on for a while?
items.a: Yes. Right-click the switch and pick Turn On For 1, 2, 4 or 8 hours: each says when it would end. While it runs, the menu says how long is left, the switch's colors drain away, and a note drops down five minutes before the end. No Time Limit keeps it on. From a terminal, wham on 2h, or wham run before a command to stay awake just while it runs.

items.q: Will my Mac overheat in a bag?
items.a: Wham will not let it cook: when macOS calls your Mac critically hot, Wham turns off and lets it sleep. Still, a busy laptop in a closed bag has nowhere to put its heat, and Wham is meant for desks, docks and shelves, where air can move. Before you pack up, flip it off and your Mac sleeps when you close it, like it always did.

Wham itself costs next to nothing. But an awake Mac drains its battery like an awake Mac, lid closed or not, so on battery Wham lets go at 10%, or at 5, 20 or 30% if you change its Battery Limit: your Mac sleeps with your work saved instead of running flat. For long jobs, plug it in.

items.q: Is my Mac locked with the lid closed?
items.a: As it always is. With no other display, Wham turns the built-in screen off a few seconds after you close the lid, and your Mac locks as your Lock Screen settings say. With a monitor plugged in, Wham leaves the screens alone.

items.q: Do I need an external display, a keyboard or power?
items.a: No. That is what macOS asks for its own “clamshell mode”, and Wham does not need any of it. Close the lid on a bare laptop and it stays awake.

items.q: What happens when I quit Wham?
items.a: Sleep comes back. Quitting turns the setting off on the way out, whether you quit from its menu (right-click the switch), from a script, or by logging out. And if Wham ever goes away without quitting, a crash or a force quit, its watchdog gives sleep back within a second.

Yes. A few times a day it asks GitHub for the latest version, checks that its developer signed it, and swaps it in, with the switch left as it was. Check for Updates in its menu does it right away. Turn off Update Automatically and Wham only tells you, in its menu, when a new version is out. What changed in each one: <changelog>What's new</changelog>.

Quit Wham from its menu, which gives sleep back, then drag Wham from Applications to the Trash. For a full cleanup, including the password rule, use the one-line uninstaller under <dev>For developers</dev>.

items.q: Why not the Mac App Store?
items.a: App Store apps live in a sandbox, and a sandboxed app cannot change the Mac's sleep setting. The ones that try settle for asking macOS to stay up, which is exactly what stops working when you close the lid.

changelog.heading: What's new
changelog.lead: Every version of Wham, newest first. Wham updates itself, so yours is likely the newest already: right-click the switch and its number is next to About Wham.

items: Check for Updates, in the menu, looks for a new version right away: it installs it, or tells you that you already have the latest.
With Update Automatically off, Wham installs nothing on its own, but its menu still tells you when a new version is out, one click away.
After an update, a note under the switch says which version you now have, and What's New in the menu shows what changed in each one.
Each length in Turn On For says when it would end.
Once on, the menu says until when your Mac stays awake, and how long is left.
No Time Limit, under the lengths, keeps a timed session going until you turn it off.
The switch's colors drain away as a timed session runs.
A note drops down five minutes before a timed session ends.
Battery Limit, in the menu: on battery, let your Mac sleep at 5, 10, 20 or 30%.
The menu opens whole, right under the switch, notch or not.
Turn On For 1, 2, 4 or 8 hours, from the menu.
On battery at 10%, or when your Mac gets critically hot, Wham lets it sleep and says why.
If Wham ever goes away without quitting, a crash or a force quit, your Mac gets its sleep back within a second.
With the lid closed and no other screen, the built-in screen turns off.
From a terminal: wham on 2h, and wham run before a command to stay awake just while it runs.
Wham updates itself, a few times a day. Update Automatically, in the menu, turns that off.
One switch in the menu bar, with the sun or the moon in its knob, rolling as it slides.
A new icon: the pixel sun, now smiling.
The first version: a switch in the menu bar that keeps your Mac awake, even with the lid closed. Click it again and your Mac sleeps as usual.
A note under the switch says what your Mac will do now, with a little sound you can turn off.
Wham opens at login, and offers to move itself to Applications when opened from the download.
Signed by its developer and notarized by Apple. From a terminal, wham on and wham off.
